# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 108 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)

**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Codex Athous, Shepherd of Hermas 108 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_108_page_001.jpg

---

## Similitude 9 — Why Some Repent and Others Don't

**1** When he had finished explaining the tower allegory, I asked him about the round stones from the deep that were fitted into the tower — and about those who were fitted in after being reshaped. **2** "As I've said," he told me, "all of them will prove useful to the building. The round ones from the deep also had to be placed in the building. **3** But they had to be cut first in order to fit with the others — and that's what caused the delay. **4** I'm genuinely glad they repented when they heard my words, and so they were cut and placed in the building. **5** Those who didn't repent — they perished. The ones cut away by the stone-cutters are dead. As for those still living who haven't been reshaped yet — if they submit to the cutting, they'll live. If not, they'll die." **6** "Lord," I said, "why is it that some people repent when they hear this, and others don't?" **7** "Because those who have no goodness left in them can't repent," he said. "The hardness of their hearts and their addictions to evil desires have dried all the goodness out of them. But those who still have goodness in them — they repent. **8** Because genuine understanding lives in the hearts of those who repent, they repent quickly and their inner goodness doesn't dry up." **9** I then asked about the cracked stones and how they got their cracks. "Were they cracked from the start?" **10** "No," he said, "those cracks came later. Their repentance wasn't wholehearted — so the cracks remain and they're not fully healed." **11** "But if they repent wholeheartedly — can they be made whole?" "Yes," he said, "wholehearted repentance makes them whole."

---

*PNEUMA renders "goodness drying up" under hardness as a vivid psychological image — the moral life as organic, subject to desiccation when starved of the moisture of repentance.*
